definition: Existing, occurring, or living beneath the snow, especially in the sheltered space between a snow cover and the ground.
etymology: A compact scientific coinage from Latin sub, “under,” and niveus, “snowy,” from nix, “snow.” It names the hidden little world that forms when winter’s snow becomes a roof.
usage: As November cools, voles begin to rely on the subnivean shelter that deeper snow will provide.
